use: Counts one person, and with de means on your own: hitori de.

example.romaji: Kyou wa hitori de iku yo.
example.english: I'm going on my own today.

examplePolite.ja: 今日は一人で行きます。

notes: Not ichinin. Hitorikko is an only child; hitorigurashi is living alone.

english: two people; the two of them; a couple
use: Futari de means just the two of us or them.

example.ja: 二人で飲みに行かない？
example.english: Want to grab a drink, just the two of us?

examplePolite.romaji: Futari de nomi ni ikimasen ka.
examplePolite.ja: 二人で飲みに行きませんか。
examplePolite.english: Shall the two of us go for a drink?

notes: Not ninin. Often means a couple: futari no jikan = time for the two of them.

name: Counting people from three
formation: number + -nin: sannin, gonin, rokunin, nananin, hachinin, kyuunin, juunin; four is yonin
english: three people (and from three up: number + -nin)
use: Regular from three on, except yonin for four.

example.english: The three of us ate together.

examplePolite.ja: 三人でご飯を食べました。
examplePolite.english: The three of us had a meal together.

notes: Seven is nananin or shichinin; nine is kyuunin, rarely kunin.

use: The one irregular count of people from three up.

example.romaji: Uchi wa yonin kazoku da yo.

examplePolite.english: We are a family of four.

notes: One n only: not yonnin, and never shinin.

use: Asks how many people; restaurant staff ask the same thing as nanmei sama desu ka.

example.english: How many people are coming today?

examplePolite.english: How many people are coming today?

notes: The same kanji read nanijin asks someone's nationality.
For two things, both is ryouhou. Three people works the same: sannin tomo.

use: Stresses every individual, not the group.

example.romaji: Hitori hitori kangae ga chigau yo.
example.ja: 一人一人考えが違うよ。

examplePolite.ja: 一人一人考えが違います。

use: Tatta stresses how few, often with a sad or surprised tone.

example.romaji: Kita no wa tatta hitori datta.
example.ja: 来たのはたった一人だった。

examplePolite.romaji: Kita no wa tatta hitori deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 来たのはたった一人でした。

notes: Tatta works with any number: tatta hyaku en = a mere 100 yen.

use: Used for bookings, parties and group plans.

examplePolite.ja: 人数を確認しておきます。
examplePolite.english: I'll confirm the number of people.

notes: Said ninzuu, with z, not ninsuu.
